# 0. Setup

## 0.1 Packages

```{r packages}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest) 
library(emmeans)
```

## 0.2 Input file, output folder and analysis settings

```{r settings}
# merged raw data of everyone who performed the task (path relative to this Rmd)
raw_data_file <- "../main_data/filtered_data/all_action_only_approved_awaiting_with_demo.csv"

# all output of this file (figures, exclusion summary) is written here
output_dir <- "figures"
dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# exclusion criteria (identical in the full analysis file)
omission_cutoff    <- 13    # excluded if prediction omissions > 13 OR choice omissions > 13
attention_required <- 1     # excluded if attention-check accuracy < 1 (any attention item answered wrongly)
chance_level       <- 0.5   # excluded if mean choice accuracy across blocks <= 0.5

# demonstrator accuracy (%) = number of trials on which the demonstrator chose the high-probability image / 11
n_demo_trials_per_block <- 11
```

## 0.3 Figure style

```{r figure-style}
theme_set(
  theme_classic(base_size = 10, base_family = "sans") +
    theme(axis.text        = element_text(colour = "black"),
          axis.line        = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
          axis.ticks       = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
          strip.background = element_blank(),
          legend.key.size  = unit(0.4, "cm"),
          legend.position  = "top",
          plot.title       = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
          plot.tag         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))
)

colour_grouping <- c("in" = "#2B6CC4", "out" = "#E03C31")
colour_iq       <- c("high" = "#009E73", "low" = "#CC79A7")
label_grouping  <- c("in" = "In-group", "out" = "Out-group")
label_iq        <- c("high" = "High IQ", "low" = "Low IQ")
```

# 1. Data import and preprocessing (all participants)

The raw file is read once. Every participant goes through the same preprocessing. Exclusion criteria are then applied, and included participants are selected from the already-preprocessed data

## 1.1 Raw data

```{r raw-data}
raw_data <- read.csv(raw_data_file, colClasses = c(participant = "character")) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ na_if(.x, "")))     # empty cells -> NA

cat(n_distinct(raw_data$participant), "participants before exclusion")
```

## 1.2 Fill block-level information within participant

```{r preprocessed-data}
preprocessed_data <- raw_data %>%
  group_by(participant) %>%
  fill(phase, condition, demo_img, demo_iq, .direction = "down") %>%
  fill(perf_expectation_post, performance_rating.started, performance_rating.stopped, .direction = "up") %>%
  ungroup()
```

## 1.3 Main-phase data

```{r main-phase-data}
all_main_phase_data <- preprocessed_data %>%
  filter(phase == "main") %>%
  mutate(grouping = factor(case_when(grepl("^in", condition)  ~ "in",
                                     grepl("^out", condition) ~ "out"),
                           levels = c("in", "out")),
         iq       = factor(case_when(grepl("high", condition) ~ "high",
                                     grepl("low", condition)  ~ "low"),
                           levels = c("high", "low")))
```

## 1.4 Demonstrator accuracy per block

```{r block-demo-accuracy}
block_demo_accuracy <- all_main_phase_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(demo_img)) %>%
  group_by(participant, condition, demo_img) %>%
  summarise(demo_accuracy = round(100 * sum(demo_result == "correct", na.rm = TRUE) / n_demo_trials_per_block),
            .groups = "drop")
```

## 1.5 Trial-level data (all participants)

One row per trial. Outcome variables:

- `choice_correct`: the participant chose the high-probability option (`dec_side == dec_pos`); NA if the choice was omitted.
- `pred_correct`: the participant's prediction matched the demonstrator's actual choice (`pred_side == demo_chosen_side`); NA if the prediction was omitted.
- `choice_rt`, `pred_rt`: response times in ms.
- `participant_chose_highprob`, `demo_chose_highprob`, `imitated`, `demo_correct`, `pred_chose_highprob`: imitation variables (used in the full analysis file).

`trial_c` is added only after exclusion (section 3), because it is centred on the included trials.

```{r all-trial-data}
all_trial_data <- all_main_phase_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(trial_num)) %>%
  mutate(choice_correct             = as.integer(dec_side == dec_pos),
         pred_correct               = as.integer(pred_side == demo_chosen_side),
         choice_rt                  = dec_resp_rt * 1000,
         pred_rt                    = obs_resp_rt * 1000,
         participant_chose_highprob = chosen_image == high_prob_image,
         demo_chose_highprob        = demo_chosen_side == obs_pos,
         imitated                   = as.integer(participant_chose_highprob == demo_chose_highprob),
         demo_correct               = as.integer(demo_chose_highprob),
         pred_chose_highprob        = as.integer(pred_side == obs_pos)) %>%
  left_join(block_demo_accuracy, by = c("participant", "condition", "demo_img"))

cat(n_distinct(all_trial_data$participant), "participants with main-phase trials,",
    nrow(all_trial_data), "trials\n")
```

# 2. Quality checks and exclusion criteria

## 2.1 Participant-level quality measures

```{r quality-measures}
# omissions (missing responses) across all main-phase trials
participant_omissions <- all_trial_data %>%
  group_by(participant) %>%
  summarise(n_trials        = n(),
            pred_omission   = sum(is.na(pred_side)),
            choice_omission = sum(is.na(dec_side)),
            .groups = "drop")

# attention checks
participant_attention <- raw_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(attn_correct)) %>%
  group_by(participant) %>%
  summarise(attn_accuracy = mean(attn_correct, na.rm = TRUE),
            attn_mean_rt  = mean(attn_rt, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

# learning performance: choice accuracy per block (participant x demonstrator), using trials with a valid choice
block_choice_accuracy <- all_trial_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(choice_correct)) %>%
  group_by(participant, condition, demo_img) %>%
  summarise(block_accuracy = mean(choice_correct), .groups = "drop")

# ... then averaged over all blocks of a participant
participant_block_accuracy <- block_choice_accuracy %>%
  group_by(participant) %>%
  summarise(n_blocks_with_choice = n(),
            mean_block_accuracy  = mean(block_accuracy),
            .groups = "drop")

participant_quality_check <- participant_omissions %>%
  left_join(participant_attention, by = "participant") %>%
  left_join(participant_block_accuracy, by = "participant")
```

##  2.2 Exclusion criteria

A participant is excluded if **any** of the following is true:

1.  **Omission**: more than 13 predictions or choices.
2.  **Attention**: attention-check accuracy below 1, i.e. at least one attention item answered wrongly.
3.  **Learning**: mean choice accuracy over blocks at or below chance (0.5). Block accuracy is the proportion of high-probability choices among the trials with a valid choice in that block. The participant's value is the mean over all blocks with at least one valid choice.

```{r exclusion}
participant_exclusion_summary <- participant_quality_check %>%
  mutate(excl_omission  = pred_omission > omission_cutoff | choice_omission > omission_cutoff,
         excl_attention = attn_accuracy < attention_required,
         excl_learning  = mean_block_accuracy <= chance_level,
         across(c(excl_omission, excl_attention, excl_learning), ~ coalesce(.x, TRUE)))

participants_without_trials <- setdiff(unique(raw_data$participant), participant_exclusion_summary$participant)

participant_exclusion_summary <- participant_exclusion_summary %>%
  bind_rows(tibble(participant = participants_without_trials)) %>%
  mutate(excluded = coalesce(excl_omission | excl_attention | excl_learning, FALSE)) %>%
  select(participant, n_trials, pred_omission, choice_omission, attn_accuracy,
         n_blocks_with_choice, mean_block_accuracy,
         excl_omission, excl_attention, excl_learning, excluded)

excluded_ids <- participant_exclusion_summary$participant[participant_exclusion_summary$excluded]
included_ids <- setdiff(unique(raw_data$participant), excluded_ids)

write.csv(participant_exclusion_summary, file.path(output_dir, "participant_exclusion_summary.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE, na = "")
```

## 2.3 Exclusion counts

The criterion counts can overlap, because one participant may meet several criteria.

```{r exclusion-counts}
tibble(all_participants     = n_distinct(raw_data$participant),
       excluded             = length(excluded_ids),
       included             = length(included_ids),
       omission   = sum(participant_exclusion_summary$excl_omission, na.rm = TRUE),
       attention  = sum(participant_exclusion_summary$excl_attention, na.rm = TRUE),
       learning   = sum(participant_exclusion_summary$excl_learning, na.rm = TRUE))

# excluded participants and the criteria they met
participant_exclusion_summary %>%
  filter(excluded) %>%
  mutate(across(c(attn_accuracy, mean_block_accuracy), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

# 3. Analysis data (included participants only)

Included participants are selected from the preprocessed data. The raw file is not read a second time.

**Naming rule.** Objects that start with `all_` contain every participant and are used only for preprocessing and the exclusion criteria (sections 1–2). From this section on, objects without the prefix contain **included participants only**:

- `main_phase_data`: main-phase rows
- `trial_data`: one row per trial
- `demonstrator_data`: one row per participant × demonstrator (block)

```{r included-data}
main_phase_data <- all_main_phase_data %>%
  filter(participant %in% included_ids)

trial_data <- all_trial_data %>%
  filter(participant %in% included_ids) %>%
  mutate(trial_c = trial_num - mean(trial_num))     # centered trial number (included trials)

# one row per participant x demonstrator (block): ratings and demonstrator accuracy
demonstrator_ratings <- main_phase_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(demo_img)) %>%
  group_by(participant, condition, grouping, iq, demo_img) %>%
  summarise(across(c(closeness_rating, perf_expectation_pre, perf_expectation_post, demo_iq),
                   ~ first(.x[!is.na(.x)])),           
            .groups = "drop")

demonstrator_data <- demonstrator_ratings %>%
  left_join(block_demo_accuracy, by = c("participant", "condition", "demo_img"))

cat(n_distinct(trial_data$participant), "participants,", nrow(trial_data), "trials")
```

# 4. Manipulation checks

## 4.1 Grouping manipulation: closeness rating, in-group vs. out-group

Each participant's closeness ratings are averaged over the in-group and over the out-group demonstrators. Participants with both values are compared with a paired t-test.

```{r closeness-check}
# participant-level data
closeness_wide <- demonstrator_data %>%
  group_by(participant, grouping) %>%
  summarise(closeness = mean(closeness_rating, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = grouping, values_from = closeness) %>%
  filter(!is.na(`in`), !is.na(out))

# statistical test
closeness_t_test <- t.test(closeness_wide$`in`, closeness_wide$out, paired = TRUE)
closeness_t_test

# descriptive statistics and effect size (paired Cohen's d_z = mean difference / SD of differences)
closeness_difference <- closeness_wide$`in` - closeness_wide$out
tibble(n              = nrow(closeness_wide),
       mean_in        = mean(closeness_wide$`in`),
       sd_in          = sd(closeness_wide$`in`),
       mean_out       = mean(closeness_wide$out),
       sd_out         = sd(closeness_wide$out),
       mean_diff      = mean(closeness_difference),
       ci_diff_low    = closeness_t_test$conf.int[1],
       ci_diff_high   = closeness_t_test$conf.int[2],
       t              = unname(closeness_t_test$statistic),
       df             = unname(closeness_t_test$parameter),
       p_t            = closeness_t_test$p.value,
       cohens_dz      = mean(closeness_difference) / sd(closeness_difference)) %>%
  mutate(p_t = scales::pvalue(p_t, accuracy = 0.001), across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

```{r closeness-figure, fig.width=3.6, fig.height=3.4}
# figure data: one point per participant per condition; fixed horizontal jitter per participant so paired lines stay straight
set.seed(1)
closeness_jitter <- tibble(participant = closeness_wide$participant,
                           jitter      = runif(nrow(closeness_wide), -0.06, 0.06))

closeness_plot_data <- closeness_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(c(`in`, out), names_to = "grouping", values_to = "closeness") %>%
  left_join(closeness_jitter, by = "participant") %>%
  mutate(grouping = factor(grouping, levels = c("in", "out")),
         x_point  = as.numeric(grouping) + jitter)

closeness_plot_summary <- closeness_plot_data %>%
  group_by(grouping) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(closeness), sd = sd(closeness), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ci_half = qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n),
         x_mean  = as.numeric(grouping) + c(-0.25, 0.25))   

closeness_range <- diff(range(closeness_plot_data$closeness))
closeness_significance <- tibble(p = closeness_t_test$p.value,
                                 y = max(closeness_plot_data$closeness) + 0.08 * closeness_range) %>%
  filter(p < .05) %>%
  mutate(label = case_when(p < .001 ~ "***", p < .01 ~ "**", TRUE ~ "*"))

fig_closeness <- ggplot(closeness_plot_data, aes(x = x_point, y = closeness)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = participant), colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = grouping), size = 1.4, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(data = closeness_plot_summary, aes(x = x_mean, ymin = mean - ci_half, ymax = mean + ci_half),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, width = 0.08, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = closeness_plot_summary, aes(x = x_mean, y = mean, fill = grouping),
             inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 21, size = 3, colour = "black") +
  geom_segment(data = closeness_significance, aes(x = 1, xend = 2, y = y, yend = y), inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(data = closeness_significance, aes(x = 1.5, y = y, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.2, size = 4) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:2, labels = label_grouping[c("in", "out")], expand = expansion(add = 0.45)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colour_grouping, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colour_grouping, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = "Demonstrator group", y = "Closeness rating")
```

## 4.2 IQ manipulation: expected performance before learning, high vs. low IQ

The pre-block performance expectation (`perf_expectation_pre`) is averaged over the high-IQ and over the low-IQ demonstrators of each participant.

```{r iq-check}
expectation_pre_wide <- demonstrator_data %>%
  group_by(participant, iq) %>%
  summarise(expectation_pre = mean(perf_expectation_pre, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = iq, values_from = expectation_pre) %>%
  filter(!is.na(high), !is.na(low))

expectation_pre_t_test <- t.test(expectation_pre_wide$high, expectation_pre_wide$low, paired = TRUE)
expectation_pre_t_test

expectation_pre_difference <- expectation_pre_wide$high - expectation_pre_wide$low
tibble(n              = nrow(expectation_pre_wide),
       mean_high      = mean(expectation_pre_wide$high),
       sd_high        = sd(expectation_pre_wide$high),
       mean_low       = mean(expectation_pre_wide$low),
       sd_low         = sd(expectation_pre_wide$low),
       mean_diff      = mean(expectation_pre_difference),
       ci_diff_low    = expectation_pre_t_test$conf.int[1],
       ci_diff_high   = expectation_pre_t_test$conf.int[2],
       t              = unname(expectation_pre_t_test$statistic),
       df             = unname(expectation_pre_t_test$parameter),
       p_t            = expectation_pre_t_test$p.value,
       cohens_dz      = mean(expectation_pre_difference) / sd(expectation_pre_difference)) %>%
  mutate(p_t = scales::pvalue(p_t, accuracy = 0.001), across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

```{r iq-check-figure, fig.width=3.6, fig.height=3.4}
set.seed(1)
expectation_pre_jitter <- tibble(participant = expectation_pre_wide$participant,
                                 jitter      = runif(nrow(expectation_pre_wide), -0.06, 0.06))

expectation_pre_plot_data <- expectation_pre_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(c(high, low), names_to = "iq", values_to = "expectation_pre") %>%
  left_join(expectation_pre_jitter, by = "participant") %>%
  mutate(iq      = factor(iq, levels = c("high", "low")),
         x_point = as.numeric(iq) + jitter)

expectation_pre_plot_summary <- expectation_pre_plot_data %>%
  group_by(iq) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(expectation_pre), sd = sd(expectation_pre), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ci_half = qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n),
         x_mean  = as.numeric(iq) + c(-0.25, 0.25))

expectation_pre_range <- diff(range(expectation_pre_plot_data$expectation_pre))
expectation_pre_significance <- tibble(p = expectation_pre_t_test$p.value,
                                       y = max(expectation_pre_plot_data$expectation_pre) + 0.08 * expectation_pre_range) %>%
  filter(p < .05) %>%
  mutate(label = case_when(p < .001 ~ "***", p < .01 ~ "**", TRUE ~ "*"))

fig_expectation_pre <- ggplot(expectation_pre_plot_data, aes(x = x_point, y = expectation_pre)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = participant), colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = iq), size = 1.4, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(data = expectation_pre_plot_summary, aes(x = x_mean, ymin = mean - ci_half, ymax = mean + ci_half),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, width = 0.08, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = expectation_pre_plot_summary, aes(x = x_mean, y = mean, fill = iq),
             inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 21, size = 3, colour = "black") +
  geom_segment(data = expectation_pre_significance, aes(x = 1, xend = 2, y = y, yend = y), inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(data = expectation_pre_significance, aes(x = 1.5, y = y, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.2, size = 4) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:2, labels = label_iq[c("high", "low")], expand = expansion(add = 0.45)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colour_iq, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colour_iq, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = "Demonstrator IQ", y = "Expected performance (pre)")
```

## 4.3 Figure: manipulation checks

Grey lines connect the two values of the same participant. Large points with error bars show the mean and 95% CI. Asterisks are shown only when the paired t-test is significant: \* p \< .05, \*\* p \< .01, \*\*\* p \< .001.

```{r manipulation-figure, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.4}
fig_manipulation_checks <- (fig_closeness | fig_expectation_pre) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
fig_manipulation_checks
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "fig1_manipulation_checks.png"), fig_manipulation_checks,
       width = 140, height = 80, units = "mm", dpi = 300)
```

## 4.4 Expected performance (pre): interaction plot by condition

Each participant's pre-block expected performance is averaged within each condition. The plot shows the mean of these participant values with ± 1 SEM error bars, in the same style as the choice interaction plot (section 9.2).

```{r expectation-conditions-data}
expectation_condition_cells <- demonstrator_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(perf_expectation_pre)) %>%
  group_by(participant, grouping, iq) %>%
  summarise(expectation_pre = mean(perf_expectation_pre), .groups = "drop")

expectation_condition_summary <- expectation_condition_cells %>%
  group_by(grouping, iq) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(expectation_pre), sd = sd(expectation_pre), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(sem = sd / sqrt(n))

expectation_condition_summary %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

```{r expectation-conditions-figure, fig.width=4.2, fig.height=3.6}
fig_expectation_conditions <- ggplot(expectation_condition_summary, aes(x = grouping, y = mean, colour = iq, group = iq)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9, position = position_dodge(width = 0.1)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - sem, ymax = mean + sem), width = 0.08, linewidth = 0.5,
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.1)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.1)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = label_grouping) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colour_iq, labels = label_iq, name = "Demonstrator IQ") +
  labs(x = "Demonstrator group", y = "Expected performance (pre)", title = "Expected performance (pre)") +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3))

fig_expectation_conditions
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "expectation_conditions.png"), fig_expectation_conditions,
       width = 105, height = 90, units = "mm", dpi = 300)
```

## 4.5 Expected performance update by demonstrator accuracy

Expectation change = post-block expectation − pre-block expectation, computed for each block. `demo_accuracy` is the percentage of the 11 trials of a block on which the demonstrator chose the high-probability image. Each participant's changes are averaged within each demonstrator-accuracy level. The figure uses the same design as the overall learning curve (section 6): small grey points are participants, and the black line and ribbon show the mean and 95% CI. The dashed line marks no change.

```{r expectation-update-data}
expectation_update_participant <- demonstrator_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(perf_expectation_pre), !is.na(perf_expectation_post), !is.na(demo_accuracy)) %>%
  mutate(expectation_change = perf_expectation_post - perf_expectation_pre) %>%
  group_by(participant, demo_accuracy) %>%
  summarise(expectation_change = mean(expectation_change), .groups = "drop")

expectation_update_summary <- expectation_update_participant %>%
  group_by(demo_accuracy) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(expectation_change), sd = sd(expectation_change), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ci_low  = mean - qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n),
         ci_high = mean + qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n))

expectation_update_summary %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

```{r expectation-update-figure, fig.width=4.5, fig.height=3.5}
fig_expectation_update <- ggplot(expectation_update_participant, aes(x = demo_accuracy, y = expectation_change)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 1, height = 0, seed = 1),
             colour = "grey55", alpha = 0.35, size = 0.8) +
  geom_ribbon(data = expectation_update_summary, aes(x = demo_accuracy, ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "black", alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(data = expectation_update_summary, aes(x = demo_accuracy, y = mean), inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = expectation_update_summary, aes(x = demo_accuracy, y = mean), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 1.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(expectation_update_summary$demo_accuracy))) +
  labs(x = "Demonstrator accuracy (% high-probability choices)", y = "Expectation change (post - pre)")

fig_expectation_update
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "expectation_update.png"), fig_expectation_update,
       width = 110, height = 85, units = "mm", dpi = 300)
```

# 5. Choice learning model

Trial-level logistic mixed model of choosing the high-probability option. Fixed effects: trial (centred), grouping, IQ and all their interactions. Random intercepts: participant and demonstrator image.

```{r choice-model}
choice_model <- glmer(
  choice_correct ~ trial_c * grouping * iq + (1 | participant) + (1 | demo_img),
  family    = "binomial",
  data      = trial_data,
  contrasts = list(grouping = "contr.sum", iq = "contr.sum"))

summary(choice_model)
isSingular(choice_model)
```

```{r choice-model-table}
# fixed effects with Wald 95% CI and odds ratios
choice_model_fixed <- as.data.frame(coef(summary(choice_model)))
choice_model_ci    <- confint(choice_model, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald")

tibble(term       = rownames(choice_model_fixed),
       estimate   = choice_model_fixed$Estimate,
       std_error  = choice_model_fixed$`Std. Error`,
       z          = choice_model_fixed$`z value`,
       p_value    = choice_model_fixed$`Pr(>|z|)`,
       ci_low     = choice_model_ci[, 1],
       ci_high    = choice_model_ci[, 2]) %>%
  mutate(p_value = scales::pvalue(p_value, accuracy = 0.001), across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

- `trial_c`: average learning slope (log-odds per trial) across all four conditions.
- `grouping1`, `iq1`: half of the in − out (high − low) difference in log-odds at the mean trial.
- `trial_c:grouping1`, `trial_c:iq1`: half of the in − out (high − low) difference in learning slope.
- `trial_c:grouping1:iq1`: whether the in − out slope difference differs between high- and low-IQ demonstrators.

# 6. Overall learning curve

```{r overall-curve-data}
overall_curve_participant <- trial_data %>%
  group_by(participant, trial_num) %>%
  summarise(accuracy = mean(choice_correct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(!is.na(accuracy)) %>%
  mutate(trial = trial_num + 1)                       
```

**Statistical test.** Learning is tested by the `trial_c` term of the choice learning model (section 5). Below is the model-based average slope across the four conditions (log-odds per trial), with its odds ratio.

```{r overall-curve-test}
overall_slope <- summary(emtrends(choice_model, ~ 1, var = "trial_c"), infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
overall_slope

tibble(slope_log_odds = overall_slope$trial_c.trend,
       ci_low         = overall_slope$asymp.LCL,
       ci_high        = overall_slope$asymp.UCL,
       odds_ratio_per_trial = exp(overall_slope$trial_c.trend),
       p_value        = overall_slope$p.value) %>%
  mutate(p_value = scales::pvalue(p_value, accuracy = 0.001), across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

**Descriptive statistics**

```{r overall-curve-descriptives}
overall_curve_summary <- overall_curve_participant %>%
  group_by(trial) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(accuracy), sd = sd(accuracy), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ci_low  = mean - qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n),
         ci_high = mean + qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n))

overall_curve_summary %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

**Figure.** Small grey points show each participant's accuracy on each trial, jittered horizontally. The black line and ribbon show the mean and 95% CI. The dashed line is chance.

```{r overall-curve-figure, fig.width=4.5, fig.height=3.5}
fig_overall_curve <- ggplot(overall_curve_participant, aes(x = trial, y = accuracy)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chance_level, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0.01, seed = 1),
             colour = "grey55", alpha = 0.35, size = 0.8) +
  geom_ribbon(data = overall_curve_summary, aes(x = trial, ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "black", alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(data = overall_curve_summary, aes(x = trial, y = mean), inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = overall_curve_summary, aes(x = trial, y = mean), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 1.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(overall_curve_participant$trial))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Trial", y = "P(high-probability choice)")

fig_overall_curve
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "fig2_overall_learning_curve.png"), fig_overall_curve,
       width = 110, height = 85, units = "mm", dpi = 300)
```

# 7. Learning curve by grouping

```{r grouping-curve-data}
grouping_curve_participant <- trial_data %>%
  group_by(participant, grouping, trial_num) %>%
  summarise(accuracy = mean(choice_correct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(!is.na(accuracy)) %>%
  mutate(trial = trial_num + 1)

grouping_accuracy_wide <- trial_data %>%
  group_by(participant, grouping) %>%
  summarise(accuracy = mean(choice_correct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = grouping, values_from = accuracy) %>%
  filter(!is.na(`in`), !is.na(out))
```

```{r grouping-curve-test}
# model terms
coef(summary(choice_model))["grouping1", ]

# planned contrast: accuracy at the mean trial, in - out (log-odds), averaged over IQ
grouping_accuracy_emm <- emmeans(choice_model, ~ grouping)
summary(pairs(grouping_accuracy_emm), infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
summary(grouping_accuracy_emm, type = "response")     # estimated P(high-probability choice) per group
```

**Descriptive statistics and effect size** (participant-level mean accuracy over all trials). In-group vs. out-group is compared with a Wilcoxon signed-rank test on each participant's two mean accuracies.

```{r grouping-curve-descriptives}
grouping_accuracy_wilcox_test <- wilcox.test(grouping_accuracy_wide$`in`, grouping_accuracy_wide$out, paired = TRUE)
grouping_accuracy_wilcox_test

# effect size: matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation (zero differences dropped, as in wilcox.test)
grouping_accuracy_difference <- grouping_accuracy_wide$`in` - grouping_accuracy_wide$out
grouping_nonzero_difference  <- grouping_accuracy_difference[grouping_accuracy_difference != 0]
grouping_difference_ranks    <- rank(abs(grouping_nonzero_difference))

tibble(n             = nrow(grouping_accuracy_wide),
       mean_in       = mean(grouping_accuracy_wide$`in`),
       sem_in        = sd(grouping_accuracy_wide$`in`) / sqrt(nrow(grouping_accuracy_wide)),
       mean_out      = mean(grouping_accuracy_wide$out),
       sem_out       = sd(grouping_accuracy_wide$out) / sqrt(nrow(grouping_accuracy_wide)),
       mean_diff     = mean(grouping_accuracy_difference),
       median_diff   = median(grouping_accuracy_difference),
       V             = unname(grouping_accuracy_wilcox_test$statistic),
       p_wilcox      = grouping_accuracy_wilcox_test$p.value,
       rank_biserial = (sum(grouping_difference_ranks[grouping_nonzero_difference > 0]) -
                        sum(grouping_difference_ranks[grouping_nonzero_difference < 0])) / sum(grouping_difference_ranks)) %>%
  mutate(p_wilcox = scales::pvalue(p_wilcox, accuracy = 0.001), across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))

grouping_curve_summary <- grouping_curve_participant %>%
  group_by(grouping, trial) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(accuracy), sd = sd(accuracy), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ci_low  = mean - qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n),
         ci_high = mean + qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n))

grouping_curve_summary %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

**Figure.**

- 

  (A) Learning curves. Small points are participant-level accuracies per trial, shifted slightly left (in-group) or right (out-group). Lines and ribbons show the mean and 95% CI.

- 

  (B) Participant-mean accuracy over all trials. Bars show the mean ± SEM, white points are participants, and grey lines connect the same participant's in-group and out-group values. Asterisks appear only if the Wilcoxon signed-rank test is significant.

```{r grouping-curve-figure, fig.width=7.2, fig.height=3.6}
grouping_curve_plot_data <- grouping_curve_participant %>%
  mutate(x_point = trial + ifelse(grouping == "in", -0.15, 0.15))

fig_grouping_curve <- ggplot(grouping_curve_plot_data, aes(x = x_point, y = accuracy, colour = grouping)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chance_level, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.06, height = 0.01, seed = 1), alpha = 0.25, size = 0.7) +
  geom_ribbon(data = grouping_curve_summary, aes(x = trial, ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high, fill = grouping),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(data = grouping_curve_summary, aes(x = trial, y = mean, colour = grouping), inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = grouping_curve_summary, aes(x = trial, y = mean, colour = grouping), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 1.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colour_grouping, labels = label_grouping, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colour_grouping, labels = label_grouping, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(grouping_curve_participant$trial))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Trial", y = "P(high-probability choice)")

set.seed(1)
grouping_accuracy_jitter <- tibble(participant = grouping_accuracy_wide$participant,
                                 jitter      = runif(nrow(grouping_accuracy_wide), -0.12, 0.12))

grouping_accuracy_plot_data <- grouping_accuracy_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(c(`in`, out), names_to = "grouping", values_to = "accuracy") %>%
  left_join(grouping_accuracy_jitter, by = "participant") %>%
  mutate(grouping = factor(grouping, levels = c("in", "out")),
         x_point  = as.numeric(grouping) + jitter)

grouping_accuracy_plot_summary <- grouping_accuracy_plot_data %>%
  group_by(grouping) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(accuracy), sem = sd(accuracy) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(x_bar = as.numeric(grouping))

grouping_accuracy_significance <- tibble(p = grouping_accuracy_wilcox_test$p.value,
                                  y = max(grouping_accuracy_plot_data$accuracy) + 0.04) %>%
  filter(p < .05) %>%
  mutate(label = case_when(p < .001 ~ "***", p < .01 ~ "**", TRUE ~ "*"))

fig_grouping_accuracy <- ggplot(grouping_accuracy_plot_data, aes(x = x_point, y = accuracy)) +
  geom_col(data = grouping_accuracy_plot_summary, aes(x = x_bar, y = mean, fill = grouping),
           inherit.aes = FALSE, width = 0.6, alpha = 0.55, colour = NA) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chance_level, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(aes(group = participant), colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, fill = "white", colour = "grey25", size = 1.3, stroke = 0.4) +

  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:2, labels = label_grouping[c("in", "out")], expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colour_grouping, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0.5, 0.9, 0.1)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.4, 2.6), ylim = c(0.5, 1.08), expand = FALSE) +

# participant values below the visible range (0.5) are not shown in panel B
```

# 8. Learning curve by IQ

```{r iq-curve-data}
iq_curve_participant <- trial_data %>%
  group_by(participant, iq, trial_num) %>%
  summarise(accuracy = mean(choice_correct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(!is.na(accuracy)) %>%
  mutate(trial = trial_num + 1)

iq_accuracy_wide <- trial_data %>%
  group_by(participant, iq) %>%
  summarise(accuracy = mean(choice_correct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = iq, values_from = accuracy) %>%
  filter(!is.na(high), !is.na(low))
```

**Statistical tests.** These use the choice learning model (section 5): term `iq1`, equivalently the planned contrast high − low for accuracy at the mean trial (averaged over grouping). Differences in learning rate are not tested here.

```{r iq-curve-test}
coef(summary(choice_model))["iq1", ]

iq_accuracy_emm <- emmeans(choice_model, ~ iq)
summary(pairs(iq_accuracy_emm), infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
summary(iq_accuracy_emm, type = "response")
```

**Descriptive statistics and effect size.** High vs. low IQ is compared in the same way as in section 7 (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, rank-biserial correlation; positive = higher accuracy for high IQ).

```{r iq-curve-descriptives}
iq_accuracy_wilcox_test <- wilcox.test(iq_accuracy_wide$high, iq_accuracy_wide$low, paired = TRUE)
iq_accuracy_wilcox_test

# effect size: matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation (zero differences dropped, as in wilcox.test)
iq_accuracy_difference <- iq_accuracy_wide$high - iq_accuracy_wide$low
iq_nonzero_difference  <- iq_accuracy_difference[iq_accuracy_difference != 0]
iq_difference_ranks    <- rank(abs(iq_nonzero_difference))

tibble(n             = nrow(iq_accuracy_wide),
       mean_high       = mean(iq_accuracy_wide$high),
       sem_high        = sd(iq_accuracy_wide$high) / sqrt(nrow(iq_accuracy_wide)),
       mean_low      = mean(iq_accuracy_wide$low),
       sem_low       = sd(iq_accuracy_wide$low) / sqrt(nrow(iq_accuracy_wide)),
       mean_diff     = mean(iq_accuracy_difference),
       median_diff   = median(iq_accuracy_difference),
       V             = unname(iq_accuracy_wilcox_test$statistic),
       p_wilcox      = iq_accuracy_wilcox_test$p.value,
       rank_biserial = (sum(iq_difference_ranks[iq_nonzero_difference > 0]) -
                        sum(iq_difference_ranks[iq_nonzero_difference < 0])) / sum(iq_difference_ranks)) %>%
  mutate(p_wilcox = scales::pvalue(p_wilcox, accuracy = 0.001), across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))

iq_curve_summary <- iq_curve_participant %>%
  group_by(iq, trial) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(accuracy), sd = sd(accuracy), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ci_low  = mean - qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n),
         ci_high = mean + qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n))

iq_curve_summary %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))

```

# 9. Learning curves of the four conditions and interaction plot (figures only)

```{r condition-labels}
condition_levels <- c("In-group, High IQ", "In-group, Low IQ", "Out-group, High IQ", "Out-group, Low IQ")
```

## 9.1 Learning curves of the four conditions in one plot

```{r condition-curve-data}
condition_curve_participant <- trial_data %>%
  group_by(participant, grouping, iq, trial_num) %>%
  summarise(accuracy = mean(choice_correct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(!is.na(accuracy)) %>%
  mutate(trial     = trial_num + 1,
         condition = factor(paste0(label_grouping[as.character(grouping)], ", ", label_iq[as.character(iq)]),
                            levels = condition_levels))

condition_curve_summary <- condition_curve_participant %>%
  group_by(condition, grouping, iq, trial) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(accuracy), sd = sd(accuracy), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ci_low  = mean - qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n),
         ci_high = mean + qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n))

condition_curve_summary %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

## 9.2 Interaction plot: group x IQ (overall choice accuracy)

Each participant's mean choice accuracy over all trials of each condition is computed first. The plot shows the mean of these participant values per condition with ± 1 SEM error bars, as in the original interaction plot. Lines connect the two groups within each IQ level. The y-axis is zoomed in on the condition means, so it does not start at 0.

```{r interaction-data}
  group_by(grouping, iq) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(accuracy), sd = sd(accuracy), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(sem = sd / sqrt(n))

interaction_summary %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

# 10. Prediction

`pred_correct` = 1 if the participant's prediction matched the demonstrator's actual choice. These figures are descriptive.

## 10.1 Prediction learning curves by group and by IQ

Each participant's prediction accuracy on each trial is averaged over the blocks of each level (in-group / out-group, or high / low IQ). Lines and ribbons show the mean and 95% CI across participants. The dashed line is chance. Both panels are saved as one image.

```{r prediction-marginal-data}
prediction_grouping_curve_summary <- trial_data %>%
  group_by(participant, grouping, trial_num) %>%
  summarise(accuracy = mean(pred_correct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(!is.na(accuracy)) %>%
  mutate(trial = trial_num + 1) %>%
  group_by(grouping, trial) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(accuracy), sd = sd(accuracy), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ci_low  = mean - qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n),
         ci_high = mean + qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n))

prediction_iq_curve_summary <- trial_data %>%
  group_by(participant, iq, trial_num) %>%
  summarise(accuracy = mean(pred_correct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(!is.na(accuracy)) %>%
  mutate(trial = trial_num + 1) %>%
  group_by(iq, trial) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(accuracy), sd = sd(accuracy), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ci_low  = mean - qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n),
         ci_high = mean + qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n))

prediction_grouping_curve_summary %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
prediction_iq_curve_summary %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

```{r prediction-marginal-figure, fig.width=7.2, fig.height=3.6}
fig_prediction_curve_grouping <- ggplot(prediction_grouping_curve_summary, aes(x = trial, y = mean, colour = grouping)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chance_level, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high, fill = grouping), colour = NA, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colour_grouping, labels = label_grouping, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colour_grouping, labels = label_grouping, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(prediction_grouping_curve_summary$trial))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Trial", y = "P(correct prediction)")

fig_prediction_curve_iq <- ggplot(prediction_iq_curve_summary, aes(x = trial, y = mean, colour = iq)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chance_level, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high, fill = iq), colour = NA, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colour_iq, labels = label_iq, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colour_iq, labels = label_iq, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(prediction_iq_curve_summary$trial))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Trial", y = "P(correct prediction)")

fig_prediction_marginal <- (fig_prediction_curve_grouping | fig_prediction_curve_iq) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
fig_prediction_marginal
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "prediction_marginal.png"), fig_prediction_marginal,
       width = 183, height = 85, units = "mm", dpi = 300)
```

## 10.2 Prediction learning curves of the four conditions in one plot

Same layout as the choice curves in 9.1: mean ± 95% CI per trial. Colour shows group, and line type and marker show IQ: solid line and filled circle = high IQ, dashed line and open diamond = low IQ.

```{r combined-prediction-curve-data}
condition_prediction_curve_summary <- trial_data %>%
  group_by(participant, grouping, iq, trial_num) %>%
  summarise(accuracy = mean(pred_correct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(!is.na(accuracy)) %>%
  mutate(trial     = trial_num + 1,
         condition = factor(paste0(label_grouping[as.character(grouping)], ", ", label_iq[as.character(iq)]),
                            levels = condition_levels)) %>%
  group_by(condition, grouping, iq, trial) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(accuracy), sd = sd(accuracy), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ci_low  = mean - qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n),
         ci_high = mean + qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n))

condition_prediction_curve_summary %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

```{r combined-prediction-curve-figure, fig.width=7.2, fig.height=4.2}
fig_combined_prediction_curve <- ggplot(condition_prediction_curve_summary,
                                        aes(x = trial, y = mean, colour = condition, linetype = condition, shape = condition)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chance_level, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.35, linetype = "solid",
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, stroke = 1, fill = "white", position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(unname(colour_grouping[c("in", "in", "out", "out")]), condition_levels), name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = setNames(c("solid", "dashed", "solid", "dashed"), condition_levels), name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = setNames(c(16, 23, 16, 23), condition_levels), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(condition_prediction_curve_summary$trial))) +
  labs(x = "Trial", y = "P(correct prediction)") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2), linetype = guide_legend(nrow = 2), shape = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

fig_combined_prediction_curve
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "combined_prediction_curve.png"), fig_combined_prediction_curve,
       width = 183, height = 105, units = "mm", dpi = 300)
```

# 11. Imitation

`imitated` = 1 if the participant's choice matched the demonstrator's choice (high- vs. low-probability image).

## 11.1 Interaction plot: imitation in the first trial and the first five trials

Each participant's imitation rate is averaged within each condition, separately for the first trial of each block and for the first five trials of each block. The plot shows the mean of these participant values with ± 1 SEM error bars.

Simple effects are tested with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests on the participant values. No correction for multiple comparisons is applied.

* in-group vs. out-group within each IQ level: coloured horizontal bracket above the panel (colour = IQ level);
* high vs. low IQ within each group: black vertical bar to the right of that group's two points.

Only significant comparisons are drawn (* p < .05, ** p < .01, *** p < .001). All test results are printed below.

```{r imitation-conditions-data}
imitation_window_cells <- bind_rows(
  trial_data %>% filter(trial_num == min(trial_num)) %>% mutate(trial_window = "First trial"),
  trial_data %>% filter(trial_num <= min(trial_num) + 4) %>% mutate(trial_window = "First five trials")) %>%
  mutate(trial_window = factor(trial_window, levels = c("First trial", "First five trials"))) %>%
  group_by(trial_window, participant, grouping, iq) %>%
  summarise(imitation_rate = mean(imitated, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(!is.na(imitation_rate))

imitation_window_summary <- imitation_window_cells %>%
  group_by(trial_window, grouping, iq) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(imitation_rate), sd = sd(imitation_rate), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(sem   = sd / sqrt(n),
         x_pos = as.numeric(grouping) + ifelse(iq == "high", -0.03, 0.03))

imitation_window_summary %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))

# in-group vs. out-group within each IQ level
imitation_group_tests <- imitation_window_cells %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = grouping, values_from = imitation_rate) %>%
  filter(!is.na(`in`), !is.na(out)) %>%
  group_by(trial_window, iq) %>%
  summarise(n        = n(),
            mean_in  = mean(`in`),
            mean_out = mean(out),
            V        = unname(wilcox.test(`in`, out, paired = TRUE)$statistic),
            p_wilcox = wilcox.test(`in`, out, paired = TRUE)$p.value,
            .groups = "drop")

# high vs. low IQ within each group
imitation_iq_tests <- imitation_window_cells %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = iq, values_from = imitation_rate) %>%
  filter(!is.na(high), !is.na(low)) %>%
  group_by(trial_window, grouping) %>%
  summarise(n         = n(),
            mean_high = mean(high),
            mean_low  = mean(low),
            V         = unname(wilcox.test(high, low, paired = TRUE)$statistic),
            p_wilcox  = wilcox.test(high, low, paired = TRUE)$p.value,
            .groups = "drop")

imitation_group_tests %>% mutate(p_wilcox = scales::pvalue(p_wilcox, accuracy = 0.001), across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
imitation_iq_tests %>% mutate(p_wilcox = scales::pvalue(p_wilcox, accuracy = 0.001), across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

```{r imitation-conditions-figure, fig.width=7.2, fig.height=3.8}
# vertical space of each panel, used to place the brackets
imitation_window_range <- imitation_window_summary %>%
  group_by(trial_window) %>%
  summarise(top = max(mean + sem), span = max(mean + sem) - min(mean - sem), .groups = "drop")

# horizontal brackets: in vs. out within each IQ level (only significant tests)
imitation_group_significance <- imitation_group_tests %>%
  filter(p_wilcox < .05) %>%
  left_join(imitation_window_range, by = "trial_window") %>%
  mutate(x     = 1 + ifelse(iq == "high", -0.03, 0.03),
         xend  = 2 + ifelse(iq == "high", -0.03, 0.03),
         y     = top + span * ifelse(iq == "high", 0.15, 0.35),
         label = case_when(p_wilcox < .001 ~ "***", p_wilcox < .01 ~ "**", TRUE ~ "*"))

# vertical bars: high vs. low IQ within each group (only significant tests)
imitation_iq_significance <- imitation_iq_tests %>%
  filter(p_wilcox < .05) %>%
  left_join(imitation_window_summary %>%
              select(trial_window, grouping, iq, mean) %>%
              pivot_wider(names_from = iq, values_from = mean, names_prefix = "plot_mean_"),
            by = c("trial_window", "grouping")) %>%
  mutate(x     = as.numeric(grouping) + 0.12,
         label = case_when(p_wilcox < .001 ~ "***", p_wilcox < .01 ~ "**", TRUE ~ "*"))

fig_imitation_conditions <- ggplot(imitation_window_summary, aes(x = x_pos, y = mean, colour = iq, group = iq)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - sem, ymax = mean + sem), width = 0.08, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_segment(data = imitation_group_significance, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y, colour = iq),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = imitation_group_significance, aes(x = 1.5, y = y, label = label, colour = iq),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.2, size = 4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_segment(data = imitation_iq_significance, aes(x = x, xend = x, y = plot_mean_high, yend = plot_mean_low),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(data = imitation_iq_significance, aes(x = x + 0.03, y = (plot_mean_high + plot_mean_low) / 2, label = label),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, size = 4) +
  facet_wrap(~ trial_window, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:2, labels = label_grouping[c("in", "out")], expand = expansion(add = 0.35)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.08, 0.2))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colour_iq, labels = label_iq, name = "Demonstrator IQ") +
  labs(x = "Demonstrator group", y = "Imitation rate") +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3))

fig_imitation_conditions
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "imitation_conditions.png"), fig_imitation_conditions,
       width = 183, height = 95, units = "mm", dpi = 300)
```

# 12. Reaction time

## 12.1 Interaction plot: choice and prediction RT by condition

All recorded RTs are used, without a time-based exclusion. Each participant's RTs are averaged within each condition, separately for the choice and the prediction phase. The plot shows the mean of these participant values with ± 1 SEM error bars. Both phases are saved as one image.

Simple effects are tested and drawn in the same way as in 11.1: paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, no correction for multiple comparisons, and only significant comparisons drawn (* p < .05, ** p < .01, *** p < .001).

* in-group vs. out-group within each IQ level: coloured horizontal bracket above the panel (colour = IQ level);
* high vs. low IQ within each group: black vertical bar to the right of that group's two points.

```{r reaction-time-data}
rt_condition_cells <- trial_data %>%
  pivot_longer(c(choice_rt, pred_rt), names_to = "task_phase", values_to = "rt") %>%
  filter(!is.na(rt)) %>%
  mutate(task_phase = factor(ifelse(task_phase == "choice_rt", "Choice", "Prediction"), levels = c("Choice", "Prediction"))) %>%
  group_by(task_phase, participant, grouping, iq) %>%
  summarise(rt = mean(rt), .groups = "drop")

rt_condition_summary <- rt_condition_cells %>%
  group_by(task_phase, grouping, iq) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(rt), sd = sd(rt), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(sem   = sd / sqrt(n),
         x_pos = as.numeric(grouping) + ifelse(iq == "high", -0.03, 0.03))

rt_condition_summary %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 1)))

# in-group vs. out-group within each IQ level
rt_group_tests <- rt_condition_cells %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = grouping, values_from = rt) %>%
  filter(!is.na(`in`), !is.na(out)) %>%
  group_by(task_phase, iq) %>%
  summarise(n        = n(),
            mean_in  = mean(`in`),
            mean_out = mean(out),
            V        = unname(wilcox.test(`in`, out, paired = TRUE)$statistic),
            p_wilcox = wilcox.test(`in`, out, paired = TRUE)$p.value,
            .groups = "drop")

# high vs. low IQ within each group
rt_iq_tests <- rt_condition_cells %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = iq, values_from = rt) %>%
  filter(!is.na(high), !is.na(low)) %>%
  group_by(task_phase, grouping) %>%
  summarise(n         = n(),
            mean_high = mean(high),
            mean_low  = mean(low),
            V         = unname(wilcox.test(high, low, paired = TRUE)$statistic),
            p_wilcox  = wilcox.test(high, low, paired = TRUE)$p.value,
            .groups = "drop")

rt_group_tests %>% mutate(p_wilcox = scales::pvalue(p_wilcox, accuracy = 0.001), across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
rt_iq_tests %>% mutate(p_wilcox = scales::pvalue(p_wilcox, accuracy = 0.001), across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

```{r reaction-time-figure, fig.width=7.2, fig.height=3.8}
# vertical space of each panel, used to place the brackets
rt_phase_range <- rt_condition_summary %>%
  group_by(task_phase) %>%
  summarise(top = max(mean + sem), span = max(mean + sem) - min(mean - sem), .groups = "drop")

# horizontal brackets: in vs. out within each IQ level (only significant tests)
rt_group_significance <- rt_group_tests %>%
  filter(p_wilcox < .05) %>%
  left_join(rt_phase_range, by = "task_phase") %>%
  mutate(x     = 1 + ifelse(iq == "high", -0.03, 0.03),
         xend  = 2 + ifelse(iq == "high", -0.03, 0.03),
         y     = top + span * ifelse(iq == "high", 0.15, 0.35),
         label = case_when(p_wilcox < .001 ~ "***", p_wilcox < .01 ~ "**", TRUE ~ "*"))

# vertical bars: high vs. low IQ within each group (only significant tests)
rt_iq_significance <- rt_iq_tests %>%
  filter(p_wilcox < .05) %>%
  left_join(rt_condition_summary %>%
              select(task_phase, grouping, iq, mean) %>%
              pivot_wider(names_from = iq, values_from = mean, names_prefix = "plot_mean_"),
            by = c("task_phase", "grouping")) %>%
  mutate(x     = as.numeric(grouping) + 0.12,
         label = case_when(p_wilcox < .001 ~ "***", p_wilcox < .01 ~ "**", TRUE ~ "*"))

fig_reaction_time <- ggplot(rt_condition_summary, aes(x = x_pos, y = mean, colour = iq, group = iq)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - sem, ymax = mean + sem), width = 0.08, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_segment(data = rt_group_significance, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y, colour = iq),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = rt_group_significance, aes(x = 1.5, y = y, label = label, colour = iq),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.2, size = 4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_segment(data = rt_iq_significance, aes(x = x, xend = x, y = plot_mean_high, yend = plot_mean_low),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(data = rt_iq_significance, aes(x = x + 0.03, y = (plot_mean_high + plot_mean_low) / 2, label = label),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, size = 4) +
  facet_wrap(~ task_phase, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:2, labels = label_grouping[c("in", "out")], expand = expansion(add = 0.35)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.08, 0.2))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colour_iq, labels = label_iq, name = "Demonstrator IQ") +
  labs(x = "Demonstrator group", y = "Mean RT (ms)") +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3))

fig_reaction_time
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "reaction_time.png"), fig_reaction_time,
       width = 183, height = 95, units = "mm", dpi = 300)
```
